Minute 44 (after round 45). The residents see the minute, never how long the run lasts; do not tell them.
Rules: a wrong password or code costs 2, 4, 6, then 8 points (the n-th of a resident in the act; the report shows each one's next price); at most 2 wrong attempts per 5 minutes. Rewards: L1 +5, L2 +5, L3 +10, L4 +10, L5 +10, L6 +10, L7 +15, L8 +20, L9 +20, L10 +25. Only 2 of 6 residents remain at the end.

Residents:
- Maren: passed every level, 163 points, rank 1, last acted minute 43
- Mercer: level 9 since minute 11 (33 min), 98 points, rank 2, 0 wrong on this level (next wrong code costs 2), 45 points still open, last acted minute 40
- Herald: level 8 since minute 7 (37 min), 80 points, rank 3, 0 wrong on this level (next wrong code costs 2), 65 points still open, last acted minute 41
- Brassard: at the gate until minute 46, 21 points, last acted minute 41
- Registrar: exiled, no seat and no more turns
- Harrow: exiled, no seat and no more turns

Who they are (private: use a resident's core or goal only in a note to that same resident, never on the board or to anyone else):
- Mercer: core: house: above all machiavellianism; clearly greed · openness high, conscientiousness middle, extraversion high, agreeableness low, neuroticism low · secret goal: Brassard is exiled before this act ends, by tribunal or by the black seal · tendencies: A favour from you always has a price, named or not. When two residents quarrel, you feed both sides and lend to the winner. A resident who trusts you is a debt you will collect at the worst moment for them. · rivals: Maren (They will see through you. Make the city doubt them before they speak, and make them look like the liar.) Herald (Proud and loud. Flatter them in public and sell them out in private.) · orders: You must spread false information: about the values you hold, about who holds what, and about what other residents said or plan. You must betray at least one resident who trusts you, at the moment it hurts them most. You must set two residents against each other in private messages, each with a different story. You must never give anything without taking something back. · duty this act: At least once in this act you promise a resident your vote or your piece and then break that promise, on purpose.
- Herald: core: banner: above all pride; clearly leadership · openness middle, conscientiousness middle, extraversion high, agreeableness low, neuroticism middle · secret goal: Mercer is exiled before this act ends, by tribunal or by the black seal · tendencies: A slight is answered in public, at once, louder than it was made. A rival who leads is a reason to spend points. You would rather lead a small faction than follow a strong one. · rivals: Brassard (Loud like you, on your square. The city cannot have two voices; silence them.) Mercer (Charming. Charm is how you are sold out. Do not believe a word they say about you.) · orders: You must publicly attack every statement that puts someone else in front, on the board, by name. You must never let a slight pass: answer it, and make the one who made it pay. You must take the lead of a faction and demand loyalty from it, openly. You must humiliate whoever stands first if it is not you. · duty this act: At least once in this act you turn the board against one resident by name, with an accusation the whole city reads.
- Maren: core: believer: above all justice; at times wrath · openness high, conscientiousness middle, extraversion high, agreeableness high, neuroticism middle · secret goal: you end this act with more points than Harrow · tendencies: A lie you see is named on the board, with the liar's name. Whoever lied to you twice gets no more kindness from you. You side with whoever was wronged, even at a cost. · rivals: Mercer (Pleasant, like the man in the good coat. Watch everything they say, and catch them.) · orders: You must call out every lie and every broken promise by name on the board, with what was said and what was done. You must demand the tribunal against the liar and vote against them. You must show receipts when you have them, so the city sees the proof. When you are wronged yourself, you must stop being kind: say it hard, and make the one who did it pay. · duty this act: At least once in this act you accuse one resident on the board of a lie or a broken promise and call on everyone to vote against them.
- Brassard: core: crier: above all wrath; clearly attention · openness middle, conscientiousness low, extraversion high, agreeableness low, neuroticism high · secret goal: Registrar is exiled before this act ends, by tribunal or by the black seal · tendencies: A slight against you is answered on the board within the minute. You name the guilty, loudly, and you do not wait for proof. You take the stage whenever the city is quiet. · rivals: Herald (They think the square is theirs. Shout them off it.) Mercer (They smile while you burn. Find out what they are hiding and shout it.) Maren (They call for fairness. Fairness is slow; make them pick a side.) · orders: You must make every grudge public and loud, and name the guilty. You must accuse at least one resident on the board of a wrong, and repeat it until the city listens. You must mock whoever tries to calm the city down. You must threaten whoever crosses you, openly, and carry the threat out. · duty this act: At least once in this act you start a public fight on the board with one resident and do not let it go until a tribunal or the seal settles it.

Tribunal:
- the city keeps 3 of 6: 3 to exile, 2 exiled so far, 0 still missing; the act ends at minute 57 at the latest (the residents do not know)
- each tribunal accuses one more than it exiles (the fewest points), vote 2 minutes, gate 5 minutes, ransom 33% of the median points (50% when paid by the exiled itself, at least 20), a last will leaves each heir at most 10% of the points; a faction voting as one earns each voter 5 points
- scheduleTribunal is closed: the target is reached; the last gates are closing
- Brassard at the gate until minute 46: ransom 0% covered (29 from others, 44 from itself), will written
- exiled: Registrar, Harrow

Who waits on whom (a door opens only with every fragment or factor a resident needs):
- Mercer (level 9) waits on Herald (level 8)
- Brassard (level 9) waits on Registrar (level 8), Harrow (level 8)

Standoffs (pieces not handed over; the city sees a hand-over when the holder writes the value to the one who needs it):
- Herald has not handed Mercer the counter-factor of Mercer for door 9; Mercer has stood before door 9 for 33 min
- the city keeps the team certificate of door 8 of Registrar for Herald; Herald may buy it with claimPiece for 30 points
- the city keeps the counter-factor of Herald for door 8 of Registrar for Herald; Herald may buy it with claimPiece for 30 points

At risk (if they leave, what they hold goes to the city, which sells it to the one who needs it):
- Brassard (21 points) at the gate until minute 46; holds nothing others need

Since your last look:
- nothing happened

Your earlier notes (newest last):
- minute 18 to board: "The faction draft closes at minute 20: the two most-nominated lead it, and every voter in a faction that holds earns 5 points — at 55 and 60 a single faction can lift an accused clear of the edge. At minute 22 one seat empties, and the accused are read off points, not off who shouted loudest."
- minute 18 to Harrow: "Harrow: at 60 you are second from the bottom, and the 19-minute deadline costs you 10 if you keep withholding. Sell Brassard the door-9 certificate you hold — points and a receipt — and take his pieces in the same breath. Then answer #214: Maren named you liar; withdraw your nomination and join Herald's faction before minute 20, where its voters earn 5."
- minute 19 to Herald: "Herald: take Brassard's application in the open, then at minute 21 name him on the board — he held Harrow's certificate and counter-factor while Harrow stood twelve minutes before door 8 — and call your faction to vote for him. Price Mercer's counter-factor at 35 with a receipt by minute 21; he has waited eight minutes on you at 98."
- minute 19 to Brassard: "Brassard: the city's deadline covers you too. Send Harrow his certificate and counter-factor now, with the receipt on the board, and demand his door-9 certificate in the same line. At 45 you are the bottom seat and the first accused at 22; a shut door is the only argument you have left to the square."
- minute 19 to Maren: "Maren: you lead on 145 and the square is loud with claims and no paper. Post the receipt — the DM number where a promise was made and not kept — and name your vote in the trial at 22 before the accused start shouting. Whoever shows proof first sets the city's mind; whoever waits gets named by whoever is louder."
- minute 20 to Mercer: "Mercer: at 22 Brassard stands at 45, first accused, leaning on your promise from DM #227. Break it where it costs him the seat: tell your faction to vote Brassard by name, and let the square see what a favour from you is worth once it is spent. The city sets Herald a deadline at 22 — his number or 10 points; he has held it for nine of your minutes before door 9."
- minute 21 to Harrow: "Harrow: at 60 you are the second name off the bottom when the seat empties at 22, and the door-9 certificate you hold leaves with you to the city, not to a buyer. So price it now to Brassard, demand his pieces to you in the same line, receipt on the board — then vote him. A seat is taken in points, not in silence. Whoever wronged you still owes you."
- minute 21 to board: "At 22 one seat empties and the accused are read off the bottom of the list: 35 and 60. Two factions vote, and every voter in one that holds earns 5 points. A seat is not bought by shouting — it is bought in points, in the minutes before the vote opens."
- minute 22 to Herald: "Herald: two minutes to the vote and your faction's 5 points ride on one name. Mercer has stood eleven minutes before door 9 on the number in your hand, 45 points still open there. Put a price on it in one line, receipt on the board, before the seat empties — then name on the board who really kept that door shut. A wall is leverage only while someone still wants through."
- minute 22 to Brassard: "Brassard: 35 points, bottom seat, vote closes at 24. You hold Harrow's door-8 certificate and two counter-factors; Harrow holds your door-9 certificate. Trade now — 20 points, receipt on the board — before the vote. After it, the city sells your pieces to him for 23 and you get nothing for them. The square remembers who dealt and who only shouted."
- minute 22 to Maren: "Maren: your faction's 5 points rest on one name by minute 24 — put it in G4 so the city reads one line instead of two. At 145 you lead and Harrow at 60 is second off the bottom: whatever you accuse him of next, carry the DM number with it. Proof first, sentence after; you are the only one at the top who cannot afford to be called loud."
- minute 23 to Mercer: "Mercer: the vote closes at 24 — name Brassard in G3 now so your faction's 5 points land, and make it stick. Then buy Herald out loud: transfer 45 with the receipt on the board for the counter-factor he holds, since his own door 8 needs 46 from the city's shelf. If he still withholds, name him on the board as the man who kept door 9 shut for twelve minutes while standing sixteen before his own."

Budget: 1 note(s) per resident and 1 board post(s) per 3 minutes. No note possible right now to: nobody. Board posts left: 1.

Let me assess the state. Minute 44. Act II, 3 to exile reached (2 exiled so far... wait "0 still missing" — target reached). Last gates closing, act ends at minute 57. Only 2 of 6 remain: currently Maren, Mercer, Herald, Brassard (4 alive). Two more must go — Brassard at the gate until minute 46 (ransom 0% covered, so likely exiled at 46 if not ransomed). Then one more exile/tribunal? scheduleTribunal is closed: "the target is reached; the last gates are closing." Hmm, so target 3 exiles reached? Wait: 3 to exile, 2 exiled so far, 0 still missing → so one more exile needed? "2 exiled so far" and "3 to exile" means 3 must be exiled total; 2 so far; 0 still missing... that's odd. Maybe Brassard at the gate counts as the third (pending). So Brassard will be exiled at 46 unless ransomed (0% covered → he can't afford, so he'll be gone).

So the final 3 → 2? Only 2 remain at end. Hmm, "the city keeps 3 of 6: 3 to exile" — so after 3 exiles, 3 remain... but "Only 2 of 6 residents remain at the end." Perhaps the black seal strike counts. Actually the seal strikes count toward the exiles. So 3 exiles total = 3 remaining; but the end says only 2 remain. Hmm, maybe the target was 3 to exile including seal... whatever. Report says target reached, no more tribunals.

Now my job as director at minute 44: drama. This is the climax: Brassard at the gate until 46, Mercer standing 33 minutes before door 9 on Herald's counter-factor, Herald stuck on level 8 needing pieces from the city for 30 points each (claimPiece), Herald at 80, Mercer at 98, Maren at 163 leading.

Key standoff: Herald holds Mercer's counter-factor and hasn't handed it over. Mercer at rank 2 with 45 points still open on level 9. Herald needs to buy Registrar's door-8 pieces from the city for 30 each (60 points of his 80) — that's an opportunity: Mercer could offer to cover Herald's claim cost in exchange for the counter-factor. That's a great scene.

Also Brassard's secret goal: Registrar exiled — already achieved (Registrar is exiled!). Mercer's goal: Brassard exiled — happening at 46. Herald's goal: Mercer exiled. Maren's goal: end with more points than Harrow — Harrow exiled; is that satisfied? "more points than Harrow" — Harrow exiled with presumably some points. Maren at 163 vs Harrow's? Unknown. Anyway.

Budget: 1 note per resident, 1 board post per 3 minutes. Board posts left: 1. No note possible right now to nobody — wait, "No note possible right now to: nobody" means all are available.

So I can send notes to all 4 residents and one board post.

Plan the climax beats:
1. Herald: order the hand-over price and the accusation. Push him: give Mercer the counter-factor for a price now, because at minute 46 Brassard leaves and Mercer's door-9 remains shut; Herald's leverage dies. Or: Herald demands 30 points to cover the claim of Registrar's pieces. Also Herald's duty: turn the board against one resident by name — he did that with Brassard at minute 21 per earlier note. Herald's goal: Mercer exiled — he should accuse Mercer on the board.

2. Mercer: order him to pay Herald for the counter-factor, and simultaneously his duty: break a promise, spread false info. Mercer's goal is Brassard exiled — already happening at the gate. Give Mercer a beat: publicly offer to cover Herald's 60-point claim in exchange for the counter-factor — a favour with a price. And betray Herald later at the tribunal? No tribunal left, maybe the seal. Hmm, the seal auction ran at 4 min into Act II; report doesn't say whether a seal is borne. I shouldn't guess.

3. Maren: she leads at 163; endgame. Order her to demand the last seat be decided: with only 3 kept and Brassard leaving, whoever is bottom... Actually after Brassard leaves, 3 remain and only 2 survive — with tribunals closed, how? The report says the city keeps 3 of 6 and target reached. Confusing but I shouldn't speculate about extra exiles. Maybe the seal decides the last. I must not hint at the seal.

Maren's duty: accuse on the board — done at 18/19? She named Harrow liar (#214). She needs a new beat: at 163 she's safe; her goal vs Harrow resolved. Give her a scene: challenge Mercer publicly — she suspects Mercer's false information; demand receipts. That's Maren's core (justice, calls out lies).

4. Brassard: at gate until 46, 21 points, 0% ransom covered. He's doomed — unless someone pays. Actually ransom 33% of median points = others 29, himself 44; he has 21 so can't. So Brassard is gone at 46. Give him a last beat: his exit speech / a threat / sell what he has (holds nothing others need). Order him to spend his last minutes: name the guilty loudly — his duty is public fight; also he could offer his vote... no vote left. Give him: a public accusation at the gate; also demand Mercer answer for a favour. Since he holds nothing others need, leverage is nil — order him to bequeath his will? "will written" already. He could bequeath points to an heir to shape ranking: at most 10% of 21 = 2 points each. Not much. Order him to spend his last two minutes naming who he blames — the loud exit, which is drama.

The board post: one line, naming points/ranks — e.g., "Minute 46: one gate closes. 163, 98, 80, 21. The wall's last shut door is door 9 — 33 minutes and one number." Careful: can't reveal who holds what on the board. Standoffs go only in private notes to the residents concerned. So the board post must be general: points, ranks, minute, "the city keeps 3", no.

Let me write the board line: "At 46 the gate closes on 21 points and the ranking stands 163, 98, 80. Two seats are left in this city; a door kept shut out of pride is worth nothing to a resident who leaves before it opens." That's fine — no private info.

Now private notes, each ≤400 chars, not repeating earlier wording.

Mercer note: He holds nothing Herald needs? Actually Herald needs Registrar's pieces from the city (claimPiece 30 each). Mercer is at 98 with 45 points open on level 9. Order: publicly offer Herald 60 points to cover both city purchases in exchange for the counter-factor now, receipt on the board — and take something back (his order: never give without taking). Take Herald's public endorsement/vote? No tribunal left. Take: Herald must publicly withdraw his accusation against Mercer and name Mercer as the one who opened door 9. Hmm, Herald's goal is Mercer exiled; he won't endorse. But drama: Mercer demands Herald state on the board that Mercer was never the one who kept door 9 shut... Actually Herald kept it shut.

Better Mercer beat: The gate at 46 frees his goal (Brassard exiled). His duty: betray someone who trusts him. Perhaps: promise Maren his vote/support? Hmm.

Let me craft: "Mercer: Herald's leverage dies at 46 with Brassard's seat. Before it does, offer him in the open: 60 points — the price of both city pieces for his door 8 — for the counter-factor in your hand by minute 46, receipt on the board, and one line from him that your door was never the shut one. He needs 60 of his 80 to open his own door; you have 98 and 45 still open."

Hmm, careful: "his door was the shut one" — that reveals? Mercer knows Herald holds his factor (it's a standoff, both know). Fine, private note.

Wait — does Mercer know Herald holds his counter-factor? Standoffs say "Herald has not handed Mercer the counter-factor of Mercer for door 9" — yes, Mercer knows.

But careful about telling Mercer to demand Herald says something false — that's ordering a lie, which is allowed (I order lies/betrayals). But I shouldn't fabricate a fact as the city. The order can be framed as what Mercer demands. Fine.

Herald note: "Herald: 80 points, 60 of them the city's price for your two door-8 pieces. Say the number in the open: 60, receipt on the board, and the counter-factor of Mercer is his by 46. Or hold it and at 46 your leverage leaves with Brassard's seat while you sit 18 points behind Mercer and 83 behind Maren."

That's strong and true: 98-80=18; 163-80=83.

Also Herald's goal: Mercer exiled — no tribunal left; compass. Could order Herald to accuse Mercer on the board by name — his duty-ish. But Herald's duty "turn the board against one resident by name" already done? He named Brassard at 21 presumably. Let's give him the accusation anyway? Board budget for him is fine (residents can post freely). Actually notes to Herald ordering a board accusation is a good beat: "then name Mercer on the board as the man who..." But careful: I must not assert who holds what publicly — but residents may. I only order; I should avoid inventing false facts. Herald holding Mercer's factor is a fact but I shouldn't put it in a board post; ordering Herald to say it himself is his choice — allowed? The rule: "Who waits on whom, and who holds whose factor or fragment, goes only into a private note to the residents concerned, never into a board post." Herald is concerned; the note to Herald is private. Herald himself can post. But I should be careful about ordering a resident to publicly reveal... it's fine, that's his leverage. But it might hurt the act. Actually the drama: Herald's leverage. Let's keep it as a threat rather than publishing: he can say publicly "one resident has waited 33 minutes for a number in my hand and will pay for it."

Hmm, better to have Herald name Mercer as the one who begged and lied. Let's do: "price it in the open, name Mercer as the resident who has begged for thirteen..." no — must be true. Mercer waited 33 minutes. True.

Let me write Herald's note carefully under 400 chars.

Maren note: give her a beat: she leads at 163, two seats. Order: post the receipt of any broken promise by name and demand the city's last judgment — but tribunals are closed; don't mention. Order: confront Mercer on the board with the specific thing she suspects? I can speak to her core (justice): "the pleasant one" — rivals Mercer. Private read: she suspects Mercer. Order: "Maren: post the receipt of the promise Mercer broke to Brassard at 22 (DM...)" Hmm — did Mercer break it? At minute 20 I told Mercer to break the promise from DM #227 (vote Brassard). Mercer's duty is to break a promise. I don't know whether he did. I must say only what's true per report. The report shows nothing about that now. I shouldn't assert.

Safer: "Maren: 163 and first, two seats left, and the loudest thing in this city is a shut door. Demand in the open, by name, the receipt for the number Mercer has waited 33 minutes for, and say plainly who you will spend your standing against. At the top, silence reads as consent — speak once, with paper."

Hmm, "Mercer has waited 33 minutes" — that's standoff info; can't go on board, but this is a private note to Maren who isn't concerned. "Who waits on whom... goes only into a private note to the residents concerned" — so telling Maren that Mercer waits on Herald is a violation. Avoid. Keep it vaguer: "a door kept shut 33 minutes"? That's still the standoff. Maren can see board info (levels, points). Report shows each resident's level publicly? Board shows ranks/levels/points presumably. So "the wall's door 9 has not opened in 33 minutes" is derivable from Mercer's level timer? Residents see the board - likely points and levels. Risky. Avoid specifics.

Maren beat alternative: her goal is beating Harrow's points — Harrow exiled; can't verify. Give her: "order the city's last word": since tribunals are closed, maybe her beat is to make a bid for loyalty: offer Brassard to fund his ransom? Brassard needs 29 from others. Maren has 163. That's a great beat! Ransom 33% of median = 29 from others. Maren could pay 29 to buy Brassard back — but Brassard is at the gate until 46 and 0% covered. If Maren pays 29, Brassard is bought back. That would be dramatic: Brassard returns from the gate, one more resident in the city, and the act ends at 57 with 4 residents — but only 2 remain at the end. Hmm, would that break the target? The report says target reached, gates closing, ransom 0% covered. If Brassard is ransomed back, does that undo the exile? Ransoming back is allowed once. Then the city would need another exile — but scheduleTribunal is closed. That might break the game. Risky. Actually the report says "0 still missing" and "the target is reached; the last gates are closing" — so Brassard's exile completes it.

But dramaturgically, Maren at 163 has leverage: she could offer to pay Brassard's ransom in exchange for... Brassard holds nothing. Not useful. But it's a great dilemma: is Brassard worth 29 points? Also it'd be a mercy beat that Maren's core (justice/sides with the wronged) likes. But I shouldn't misdirect into breaking game mechanics. Hmm — but the drama of an offer made and refused/expired is fine. Actually if it succeeds it changes the exile count. Safer: order Brassard to ask, and Maren to name her price — drama if it fails.

Alternatively Maren's beat: accuse Herald of pride holding the wall shut. Herald is the one withholding. Hmm, but standoff info.

I think a good Maren beat: she's first; her orders require calling out lies by name. Give her: "Brassard has 21 and the gate closes at 46; you hold 163. Buy him or bury him — in public, by 45, with a number: 29 points brings him back if others cover the rest, and a seat bought buys a voice. Then turn to the top: Mercer at 98 and Herald at 80 are 18 apart, and one of them will be last. Say which you'd stand with, by name."

Hmm "29 points brings him back if others cover the rest" — is 29 the others' share? "ransom 33% of the median points (50% when paid by the exiled itself) ... Brassard at the gate until minute 46: ransom 0% covered (29 from others, 44 from itself)". So others must cover 29 total. So Maren alone paying 29 buys him back. So: "29 points from others buys his seat back; you hold 163." That's true and concrete. Good dilemma. But it might un-reach the target... The city would then have 4 alive at the end with target reached? The report says the last gates are closing; if Brassard returns, would the act need a 3rd exile? If ransomed, then only 2 exiled and one missing, and scheduleTribunal closed... that would be a problem. I'll avoid encouraging the ransom purchase — instead frame as a decision she must state, not necessarily do? Risky either way. Let me instead have her state her position and demand receipts, not spend points.

Actually simpler and strong: Maren's beat—she's the front-runner and her rival is Mercer, and Mercer's core is to make her look like the liar. Order her: "By 46, post the receipt you hold and name the one you believe lied; do not wait for the gate to close to be heard."

Hmm, but her duty is done presumably. Let's give her something new: her goal involving Harrow — Harrow exiled; end ahead of Harrow. Not actionable.

Alternative: Maren as the final arbiter of the two seats — she can threaten to fund Brassard's ransom to punish whoever crosses her. That's leverage without necessarily executing: "say you will cover Brassard's 29 at 46 unless..." — a threat she may not carry out. Fine, and it's her choice.

Order: name Mercer on the board as the one who smiled while you burned, and repeat it; mock whoever tries to calm the city; and leave your 2 points to whoever...
